title: A counterexample to Hickingbotham's conjecture about $k$-ghost-edges
summary: Fix $k\in \mathbb{N}$ and let $G$ be a connected graph with $tw(G)\leq k$. We say that $xy\in E(G^c)$ is a {\em $k$-ghost-edge} of $G$ if for every tree decomposition $(T,\cB)$ of $G$ with width at most $k$, the set $\{x,y\}$ is contained in a bag of $(T,\cB)$. Although a $k$-ghost-edge of $G$ is not an edge of $G$, but it behaves like real edges with respect to tree decomposition of $G$ with width at most $k$.
